q: In a Flow Net, the flow lines and equipotential lines always intersect at:
o: Angles depending on the soil permeability
e: This is a fundamental property of potential flow. The drop in head (potential) occurs perpendicular to the direction of flow. If they didn't cross at 90⁰, there would be a component of flow along the equipotential line, which is impossible.

q: The "Vane Shear Test" is specifically recommended for determining the shear strength of:
e: Soft clays are very sensitive to disturbance. Sampling them for a Triaxial test often destroys their structure. The Vane Shear test is done in-situ (on-site) to get the undisturbed strength, which is critical for stability analysis.

q: When the water table rises above the ground surface (flooding condition), the Effective Stress in the soil at a depth 'z':
e: Deep Concept: Effective stress = Total Stress - Pore Water Pressure. When water rises above ground, both Total Stress and Pore Pressure increase by the same amount. They cancel out. Therefore, effective stress (which governs strength) does not change due to surface flooding.

q: A soil sample is considered "Well Graded" if:
o: It has a Uniformity Coefficient (C_u) close to 1
It contains particles of all sizes in good proportions
It contains particles of only one specific size
It has a high Void Ratio
e: "Well graded" means the smaller particles fill the voids between larger particles, leading to a dense, strong soil. (C_u > 4 for gravel, > 6 for sand). A soil with only one size (Option C) is "Uniformly Graded" (which is actually poorly graded for strength).

q: In "Under-Reamed Piles", the bulb (enlarged base) is provided mainly to:
o: Resist uplift forces in Black Cotton Soil
Reduce the settlement of the pile
e: While it does increase bearing, the primary reason for using under-reamed piles in expansive soils is to anchor the pile deep in the stable zone so it isn't pulled out when the surface soil swells (heaves) upwards.

q: "Creep" in concrete structures is the:
o: Time-dependent deformation under sustained constant load
Shrinkage due to loss of moisture
Thermal expansion due to heat of hydration
e: Concrete continues to deform slowly over years under its own weight or permanent loads. This "plastic flow" or creep can cause redistribution of stresses and must be accounted for in design, distinct from immediate elastic strain.

q: Which defect in timber is caused by the crushing of fibers due to the felling of the tree?
e: "Upsets" are traumatic injuries to the wood fibers caused by severe shock or compression (like dropping the tree during felling). Knots are branch bases; Shakes are cracks.

q: The "Slenderness Ratio" of a masonry wall determines its:
o: Permissibility to carry vertical loads without buckling
e: If a wall is too tall and thin (high slenderness ratio), it will fail by buckling (bending sideways) long before the material crushes. Codes limit this ratio to ensure stability.

q: For maximum discharge through a circular channel (like a sewer pipe), the depth of flow should be:
e: Counter-intuitive fact: Friction from the top surface of the pipe (wetted perimeter) slows the flow when full. The maximum velocity occurs at 0.81 D, and maximum discharge occurs at approx 0.95 D, not when full.

q: "Cavitation" in a centrifugal pump or siphon occurs when the absolute pressure at any point:
o: Falls below the vapor pressure of the liquid
Becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure
e: When pressure drops below the liquid's vapor pressure, the liquid boils at room temperature, forming vapor bubbles. When these bubbles move to high-pressure zones, they collapse (implode) violently, pitting the metal surface.

q: The "Hydraulic Gradient Line" (HGL) represents the sum of:
o: Pressure Head + Velocity Head + Datum Head

q: "Breakpoint Chlorination" is the point where:
o: Chlorine demand is completely satisfied, and residual chlorine begins to appear
Chlorine is added to remove bad taste
Chlorine is added to remove iron and manganese
The breakdown of pumps occurs due to chlorine corrosion
e: When you add chlorine, it first reacts with organics and ammonia (forming chloramines). Only after this demand is met (the "breakpoint") does free residual chlorine appear to protect the water from future contamination.

q: In a Combined Sewer System (carrying both sewage and storm water), the "Egg-Shaped" sewer section is preferred over a circular section because:
o: It provides a higher self-cleansing velocity during low (dry weather) flow
It has a larger cross-sectional area
It resists external earth pressure better
e: In dry weather, flow is very low. A wide circular bottom would spread this water thin, causing solids to settle. The narrow bottom of an egg-shape keeps the depth higher and velocity faster, ensuring the sewer stays clean even with low flow.

q: A "Reflux Valve" (or Check Valve) is used in a pipeline to:
o: Allow flow in one direction only
e: This is critical on the delivery side of a pump. When the pump stops, the water in the rising main tries to rush back. The Reflux Valve slams shut to prevent this backflow, which could damage the pump impeller. [attachment_1](attachment)
